findings.issue: isBuildRender keys on the undocumented stub hostname 'gracile-static' used by Gracile's build-time asset-collection pass; if a framework update changes it, every build silently fires the full API fan-out (species, all types, all generations) instead of failing loudly.
findings.suggestion: Guard more defensively (e.g. also skip when API_BASE_URL is unreachable or wrap in try/catch returning empty data), and cite the Gracile version/source that defines the stub URL in a comment.

findings.issue: A single module-global AbortController is shared by pokemon-browser, moves-panel and team-page, so starting one island's fragment fetch aborts another's; the abort is swallowed as a no-op, leaving stale UI.
findings.suggestion: Key controllers per island (or per URL) so concurrent fetches from different islands don't cancel each other.

findings.issue: 430-line god data module: every API type shape and every derived query (species index, types, generations, cards, team, coverage, move tables) lives in one file all five routes import; getTypeLabels() hides a fetch-all-types fan-out.
findings.suggestion: Split by resource (pokemon.ts, types.ts, moves.ts, team.ts) and keep the api.ts client as the only shared low-level module.

findings.issue: The '<n> of 6' count uses cookie names while getTeamCards drops names that don't resolve to a species, so the count can disagree with the rendered card list.
findings.suggestion: Derive the count from props.cards.length (or filter names to resolved cards before returning).

findings.issue: window 'popstate' listener is added in connectedCallback with no disconnectedCallback cleanup; benign today because the element is never unmounted, but team-page.ts:24 shows this codebase does replace elements dynamically.
findings.suggestion: Add disconnectedCallback removing the listener, or attach via AbortController stored on the instance.

findings.issue: toggleTeamMember is dead code that duplicates the add/remove logic implemented inline in team-toggle.ts:23-30.
findings.suggestion: Delete it, or have team-toggle call it so the rule lives in one place.

findings.issue: All five client islands ship on every page via the global document bundle instead of Gracile's per-route *.client.ts convention, forgoing per-route code splitting.
findings.suggestion: Move each island import into a sibling route client file (e.g. routes/(home).client.ts), or note the deliberate trade-off in a comment.

findings.issue: 'lit' is a declared direct dependency but no module in src imports it (islands are vanilla custom elements).
findings.suggestion: Either drop the dependency (Gracile brings Lit transitively) or use LitElement for the islands as the 'Gracile with Lit' stack implies.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache never removes expired entries, only rejected promises, so it grows to the size of the API snapshot and holds stale values forever.
findings.suggestion: Prune expired entries on insert (or use an LRU cap) to keep the cache's memory story explicit.

findings.issue: The moveTables template helper is exported from the route module while all other shared template helpers live in components/partials.ts, breaking the file's own convention.
findings.suggestion: Move it (with the COLUMNS constant) into components/partials.ts alongside cardList/section.

summary: A disciplined, framework-faithful Gracile 0.11.0 app: correct route/document/adapter usage, a careful cached data layer, SSR-first pages enhanced by small vanilla islands, and a team-builder feature that slots cleanly into the existing conventions. The notable debts are the undocumented 'gracile-static' build-render guard, the shared island AbortController, and the monolithic lib/data.ts. I'd merge after a nits round addressing those and the dead code.
